sample_data.method: Embedded published fixture in js/cases.js (from P02_pharmacy_expiry_public.json). Default load is PUB-01. Judges can also pick PUB-01…PUB-25 in Settings, open ?case=PUB-01, paste case JSON, or call window.applyCase(caseObj).
sample_data.reset_instructions: Reload index.html, or Settings → select PUB-01 → Load case, or open ?case=PUB-01, or run window.applyCase(window.P02_DATA.cases[0]) in the browser console. That restores today, items and mark_returned from the published case.

problem_solving_method: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS single page with no build step so judges can open index.html immediately. Classification, paisa math and returned exclusion live in js/classify.js; the UI in js/app.js calls that layer and exposes window.applyCase / window.getSnapshot plus data-testid hooks for the four counts, two scored values, returned list and per-row Return buttons.

R1.evidence: Stock list of 40+ lots (name, batch, quantity, expiry) from the published fixture; default PUB-01 has 47 items. Rendered in Inventory Registry on Dashboard and Inventory (index.html, js/cases.js, js/app.js).

R2.evidence: Dashboard risk cards split active stock into expired, 0–30 days, 31–90 days and safe, with counts. Testids: count-expired, count-expiring-30, count-expiring-90, count-safe. Buckets in js/classify.js (daysLeft < 0; 0–30 inclusive; 31–90; > 90).

R3.evidence: Return on each active row (btn-return-{id}) moves the lot off the four active groups into Returned to distributor (list-returned, count-returned). mark_returned from the case is applied on load. R-24: returned lots are excluded from active counts and value totals (js/classify.js analyze, js/app.js markReturned).

R4.evidence: Value at Risk on Expired and Expiring Soon cards: quantity × unit_price_bdt in integer paisa, shown as ৳ with two decimals. Testids: value-expired, value-expiring-soon. Expiring soon is the 0–30 group only (R-04, R-27). Also copied on Reports.

team_members.major_contribution: Implemented the MediStock console: expiry classification, paisa value-at-risk, return-to-distributor flow, published-case loader, dashboard/inventory UI and judge testids.
Owns the team GitHub repository lsh26-t007-p02 used for this problem submission.

major_design_decisions: No build / no framework so the app is one HTML file plus CSS and JS; judges do not need npm or a server (optional python -m http.server).
Keep classification and money math in js/classify.js, separate from DOM code, so bucket and paisa rules stay testable and stable.
Store money as integer paisa then format to two decimal taka, matching unit_price_bdt as purchase price (R-27).
Treat expiry as calendar-day difference at UTC midnight so day 0 and day 30 land in expiring-soon, day 31 in 90-day, day 91 in safe.
Keep paginated table rows in the DOM with class is-hidden-row so data-testid item-row-{id} and btn-return-{id} remain queryable.
Load the published JSON as js/cases.js (window.P02_DATA) because a file:// page cannot fetch a sibling JSON file.
known_limitations: GitHub Pages is not enabled; live_url currently points at the GitHub repository. Judges can open index.html in a browser or serve the folder with python -m http.server 8080.
There is no undo for Return; a returned lot stays on the returned list until a case is reloaded.
Stock is in-memory only; a full page reload restores the selected (or default PUB-01) case.
Reports is a short loss-visibility summary of the two scored taka totals, not a full export or chart pack.
Add Medicine is a local helper for demos; it is not part of the published fixture.
